decisions.reason: “Earn a place” matches 올랐다 and keeps the ranking parallel with the Fire King sentence; “become one of” is looser and not better English.
콩 심은 데에서 콩 나는 법 is like-begets-like; “you reap what you sow” is a different proverb about consequences.
우웨에엑 is a vomit sound; “bleeegh” is recognizable English onomatopoeia, unlike “uweeek.”
Folding the question into the attribution is natural English and keeps 계속 구역질.
The question now lives in the previous sentence; a separate paragraph would double it.
“You’re clearly not” is tighter deadpan after “I’m all right,” still answering 안 괜찮으시구나.
우웩 is retching; “bleegh” preserves the vomit beat that “ugh” flattens.
Cheongpung calls Taekyung 은인; 선배님 is Gong Ilhyuk. BASE wrongly uses first person; SOL’s “Don’t call him Senior” misreads 선배님은 무슨 as a title rebuke.
decisions.replacement: “Forget Senior. He’s fine. A little spit and this much will heal right up.”

decisions.reason: “Wide-eyed” is cleaner English for 눈을 부릅뜨고 without adding meaning.
Participial “forgetting his pain, he stared… before shouting” is tighter and still covers 유난히 and 고통도 잊은 채.
네놈 따위 is contemptuous; “someone like you” underplays the insult.
“Sorry to interrupt” is more spoken for 말씀 중에 죄송한데요.
“Awful lot” captures 엄청, which “a lot” undersells.
운운했으니 points at 네놈 따위; quoted “someone like you” is weaker and clunky.
SOL drops 큭, the pain-grunt before the excuse.
Glossary binds 연무장 as training ground, not hall.
격차 is “gap,” and the shorter sentence is cleaner.
BASE’s “swallowed honey” is opaque for 꿀 먹은 벙어리; SOL’s “Sure enough… clammed up” drops 그 증거로.
decisions.replacement: The proof was that the moment I offered to set it up, Gong Ilhyuk clammed up.

decisions.reason: 지혈부터 is repeated in full; “The bleeding.” breaks that nagging echo.
Isolated …… to … restyle; SOL still uses …… elsewhere, so this is churn.
“Glared at me murderously” recasts 살벌한 눈빛 without the body-part calque.
Dropping “that” is indistinguishable, not an improvement.
엮였으니 is getting entangled, not specifically “picked a fight.”
One sentence with “and” matches 아닐뿐더러 better than a split plus “also.”
SOL front-loads 이 새끼야 and loses the 어? 다 했어 end-punch.
“Went through the roof” matches 떡상 better than “took off.”
“Staunching” is a literary synonym after the chapter’s repeated “stop the bleeding.”
SOL drops 평생 (“entire”) and “clearly/obviously” is mere synonym churn.
또 is the “and now this”; SOL deletes that beat.
돌아봤다 is looking back at Taekyung; SOL drops the turn.
“Think you know” adds a challenge that 뭘 알고 계신 거예요 does not.
“That cranes bring babies” answers the question more directly without extra padding.
그게 그러니까 is “well, that’s…”; “you see” is added filler.
Splitting age and “now that he had come down” reads cleaner without changing sense.
한 번 해 보세요 must stay ambiguous so “With Benefactor?” lands; “Repeat after me” spoils the joke.
Spoken “I said repeat” is cleaner than “I said to repeat.”
“My ambitious attempt” is more natural than “begun so ambitiously,” same 야심 차게.
“Whelps” and “in the presence of” weaken 핏덩이 놈들 and stiffen 앞에 두고.
“Gotten his arm splinted” is natural English for 부목까지 댄.
“Throws his weight around just because he’s strong” is idiomatic for 힘만 믿고 까부는.
The sarcastic thanks lands better as “clearing that up” than stiff “telling me.”
SOL’s “couldn’t read the situation” is better, but it collapses 종남파라는 배경 and 오촌 당숙에 대한 믿음 into one “faith.”
decisions.replacement: I let out a deep sigh. The man was old enough to know better, yet he still couldn’t read the situation. Was his background as a member of the Zhongnan Sect, and his faith in his father’s cousin, simply too strong?

decisions.reason: “Loose mouth” is the idiom for 방정한 주둥이; SOL drops 거 and uses an unnatural collocation.
이 친구 is “this friend,” not “my friend”; “Never mind me” matches 나야 그렇다 치고.
“Coming up now” is more natural inner voice for 여기서 왜 나와.
의문을 담아 is puzzled, not confused; 입술을 뗐다 is the physical beat SOL flattens to “spoke.”
본산에 있었지 is “was at”; “lived” over-specifies a lay disciple.
Speaker tag belongs with the following line; deleting the stranded attribution is correct.
Merging “Gong Ilhyuk added with a mocking grin” into the quote is standard English.
“That’s right” matches 맞아, and “fell ill” is the natural collocation for 앓았지.
공교로운 is a pointed coincidence, “remarkable,” and the tighter relative clause is better English.
Isolated ellipsis restyle, not a prose gain.
“As tuition goes” is idiomatic for 수업료로는; “long ago” is the same 오래전에.
뛰쳐나간 in this accusation is desertion: “ran away,” not merely “ran out.”
Master said 갈 곳이 있다 and Li Feng 따라간; BASE’s “somewhere we had to go / when we arrived” invents a joint obligation.
“Accompany them on a visit” matches 중요한 자리에 끼워 줬으니까 better than “join them.”
“The one everyone knows” fits legendary 그분; “the man” is merely different.
SOL drops 곳곳 (“several places”) and 점점 (“growing”).
오랫동안 is “a long time,” not the unsupported “years.”
“That’s true. But he was still on Huashan” is spoken and still covers 남아 계셨네 and deep seclusion.
“Only after… did we” captures 후에야 better than “before we could.”
Dropping “the” before “other children” is indistinguishable.
수작을 부리는 is dirty tricks; “rigging” narrows it to fixing the match.
Bitter 재밌지 않나 is sarcastic “amusing,” not neutral “interesting.”
“Hit hard” is Taekyung’s voice for 여파는 강렬했다; BASE is stiff.
“Conversation I’d had” is natural English; “shared with him” is calqued from 나눴던.
꺼지라고 is “get the hell out”; “get lost” and “caused a scene” soften it.
그때까지만 해도 몰랐다 is “until then I hadn’t known,” not “at the time I hadn’t realized.”
Keeps the 행패-from-a-child’s-eyes explanation without quoting “caused a scene.”
행패를 부려 targets the Sword Saint; “for” is clearer than ambiguous “with.”
도 is “also/either,” not “then again”; 보통 is “ordinary,” not “normal.”
Tighter sentence, same 부지기수 / 약관 / First Rate facts.
“Fell short of being called” is exact for 고수라고 하기에는 부족하다.
“Having a fit” is the English collocation for 발작처럼; “suffering a fit” sounds medical.
약속이라도 한 듯 is the as-if-planned image; “in unison” genericizes it.
Li Feng’s 하네체 supports uncontracted “There is no proof.”
The proverb states mountains do change in ten years; “can change” and “Why should I” weaken 강산도 변하는데 / 믿어야 하나.
어떻게 장성했는지 is how the child grew up, not specifically how he looks.
Merging the address into the asking line is natural; the chill on the blade remains.
The Young Hero question was merged into the previous sentence.
Korean 네 confirms “you’re not from Huashan”; English needs “No,” not calqued “Yes.”
묻겠소 is “allow me to ask”; “you something” is extra padding.
“Handed his sword” is natural; 들고 있던 is already visible on the page.
아니 is “no,” and “suffice” matches 족하오’s register.
머뭇거리던 is hesitating; BASE’s “for a moment” is added.
짧게 보여 드릴게요 is Cheongpung’s simple “show you briefly,” not a “demonstration.”
The Korean reveals 머리부터 발끝까지 first; SOL postpones that cinematic beat.
숨결을 태우는 is stated as fact; “felt as though it would scorch” hedges it.
“The” is natural English, but SOL deletes the first-use footnote the Hanja name still needs.
The table-cleaving line is its own beat; SOL’s dash-merge also turns 단단한 탁자 into “wood.”
음식과 접시, 단단한 탁자까지 is a delayed list punch, not a clause to absorb.
깨트리는 건 is “things,” 눈치 is “noticed”; SOL’s “something/realized” is merely different.
Keep the Zaha footnote; first on-page use of the technique still needs the gloss.
